frames.narration: Day 0: v4 is released. Users are on v1 (10%), v2 (20%) and v3 (70%). Each app sends its version with every request, so the server can see who is calling.
Adoption is quick at first and then slows. After 7 days 56.9% are on v4, after 14 days 68.5%, and 8% of users never update at all.
On day 14 the team renames a field and drops the old name. Apps before v4 still look for the old name. They cannot be fixed by a deploy.
Waiting does not fix it. After 90 days users on old versions are still there, because the tail is long and some users never update. A breaking change is never safe by waiting.

The compatible way is to add. Send both fields. New clients read the new one, old clients read the old one, and a client that ignores fields it does not know never notices the extra one. No such client breaks.
Even an additive change can break a client that rejects unknown fields: v1 does. Tolerate unknown fields on both sides, or have the server omit the field for versions that cannot take it.
A security bug is found in v2. The team raises the minimum supported version to v3. The v2 and v1 apps show an update screen, with a link to the store, instead of calling the API.
The old field is removed only when the version data shows that almost nobody needs it, or after a planned forced upgrade. Until then the extra code stays.
